questions.q: Why should your workflow map the response block whose type is "text" instead of simply mapping the first item in the reply?
options: The model can return a thinking block before its answer
The first item always holds the stop reason, not the answer
The first item repeats the prompt you sent to the model
Text blocks are the only kind a platform is able to map
questions.explain: The reply is a list of content blocks, and the answer isn't always first because the model can return a thinking block before it. Mapping the text block gets you the actual answer.

questions.q: Your AI step returns a category, but the stop reason is max_tokens. What should your workflow do next?
options: Continue as normal, since a category came back
Treat it as a refusal and stop the workflow for good
Not act on it; raise the limit or shorten the input
Retry the same request until the stop reason changes
questions.explain: A max_tokens stop reason means the output was cut off at the length limit. You raise the limit or shorten the input, and you never act on partial output.

questions.q: You're adding a direct HTTP request to an AI provider in your automation platform. Which setup follows the lesson's advice?
options: Type the API key into the request headers so it's easy to change
Keep the key in the credential store and use the structured body editor
Write the body as raw JSON so you can see exactly what is being sent
Set effort to high on every step so classifications are more careful
questions.explain: The API key belongs in the platform's credential store, never typed into a step. The structured body editor keeps quotes and line breaks in customer text from breaking the request.
